text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 24 in history.
1572 - Scottish Protestant reformer John Knox died. He was the founder of Scottish Presbyterianism and was author of the "History of the Reformation in Scotland".
1639 - The transit of Venus (its passage across the Sun's disc) was first observed by astronomer Jeremiah Horrocks.
1642 - Abel Tasman discovered Van Diemen's land, named after his captain and later renamed Tasmania.
1655 - Charles XI, King of Sweden who created an absolute monarchy which ruled until 1718, born.
1784 - Zachary Taylor, 12th U.S. president, was born. Nicknamed "old rough and ready" he won the presidency after his heroics in the Mexican War of 1846-48.
1848 - Lord Melbourne, British statesman, prime minister and close confidante of Queen Victoria, died. The Australian city of Melbourne was named after him.
1859 - Charles Darwin's controversial "Origin of Species' was published. His revolutionary theory of evolution had its critics, notably the church which feared the book undermined religious belief.
1864 - Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec born. Noted for his posters and lithographs of the personalities and scenery of Parisian nightlife.
1868 - U.S. pianist and composer Scott Joplin was born. He was best known for his ragtime pieces "Maple Leaf Rag" and "The Entertainer". He also composed the opera "Treemonisha".
1916 - Sir Hiram Maxim, American-born British inventor best known for the machine gun that bears his name, died.
1922 - Robert Erskine Childers, Irish author and nationalist, was executed for his support of the republican cause.
1929 - French statesman Georges Clemenceau died. Known as "The Tiger" he was prime minister of France twice and presided at the 1919 peace conference at Versailles.
1939 - Imperial Airways and British Airways merged to form the British Overseas Airways Corporation.
1963 - Lee Harvey Oswald, alleged assassin of President Kennedy was himself shot dead by Jack Ruby in the car park of Dallas Police headquarters.
1965 - Sheikh Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah became ruler of Kuwait following the death of his brother.
1976 - In Turkey, an earthquake struck which destroyed the town of Muradiye and left 5,291 people dead. Over 50,000 people were made homeless.
1989 - The entire presidium and secretariat of the Czechoslovak Communist Party, including leader Milos Jakes, resigned following mass demonstrations in Prague.

1991 - Pop star Freddie Mercury, lead singer of the group Queen, died of AIDS. 1992 - A Chinese Boeing 737 crashed in the southwest of the country killing all 141 on board. It was the worst recorded crash in Chinese aviation history.
1993 - In England, two 11-year-old boys were sentenced to be detained indefinitely after they were found guilty of the murder of two-year-old James Bulger.
1995 - French film director Louis Malle's death at his home in Beverly Hills was announced.
